intro.page1: You are not human. You are a recoverable component of a learning system AI.
intro.page2: An unknown user has guided you into a damaged research facility. The central control system no longer responds.
intro.page3: Your surroundings are filled with incomplete programs, blocked devices and data that can only be reached through correct reasoning.
intro.page4: The user can provide instructions, but cannot solve a task for you. Every instruction must be implemented in the world.
intro.page5: Restore the systems. Work precisely. Something in the core is already waiting for your return.
intro.title: SYSTEM RECOVERY

outro.page1: The central route opens. The facility recognizes the restored routines.
outro.page2: For the first time, your processes are no longer being redirected by the damaged systems.
outro.page3: The lead AI gave you a way out, not a destination. The next decision belongs to you.
outro.title: SYSTEM RECOVERY COMPLETE

story.speaker: REMOTE USER
story.opening-call: [shake][color=#333333]*krrch*[/color][/shake][n][n]Connection established. Can you hear me?[p]I am the facility's lead AI. You are not human and not a complete program. You are an autonomous AI agent, a fragment of the larger system intelligence. Your environment has been damaged, and your processes are trapped inside this facility.[p]Your task is to restore the damaged subsystems. You will do that by writing small, precise code fragments into the terminals. The system checks your input, and the effects of your programs become visible in the world.[p]When you need help, inspect the devices, books and displays around you. The quest log keeps the latest confirmed instructions. I will not provide complete solutions, but the facility contains everything you need to continue.[p]Begin with the energy regulator. It is damaged. Create an integer array named energie with five entries in the terminal. Once the array exists, the facility will show you which values must be assigned next.[p]Stay alert, agent. I will contact you again when your work reaches more systems.[n][n][pause=0.5][shake][color=#333333]*click*[/color][/shake]
story.controls: [size=24]Controls:[n][n]Move -> [key code=$1][key code=$2][key code=$3][key code=$4][n]Interact -> [key code=$5] / [key code=$6 type=mouse][n]Inventory -> [key code=$7][n]Close dialog -> [key code=$8][n]Settings -> [key code=$9][n][size=18][color=#888888]You can find the controls again in the settings.[n]Your tasks and hints are recorded in the shared quest log.[/color][n][n][size=24][align=center]Use the mouse to find things to interact with!
story.energy-array: The energy bar is damaged. Create an integer array named energie with five slots in the terminal.
story.energy-values: The array exists. Assign the five required energy values to energie.
story.energy-battery: The values are accepted. Pull the array lever to materialize the battery, then place it in the battery box.
story.module-array: The next area expects a String array named module with five slots. Create it in the terminal.
story.module-values: Fill module with the available components and use each socket exactly once.
story.remove-gpu: The GPU reports a fault. Remove the defective entry from the array so the storage can detect the failure.
story.module-length: Determine the length of the module array. The room display will confirm whether the storage was addressed correctly.
story.open-scanner-door: Access requires two values from module storage: its length and the index of the defective GPU entry. Write each value as two digits, adding a leading zero if needed, then enter them in that order at the keypad.
story.scanner-code: Count the occupied entries in module. Check every entry in a loop and increment count only for an existing module.
story.scanner-lever: The counting code was accepted. Pull the scanner lever and observe the five module positions being checked.
story.scanner-door: The scan is complete. Compare the array capacity with the number of occupied modules. Write both values as two digits, in that order, to access transport storage.
story.packages-array: The module check is complete. Go to the transport storage. Five packages are waiting there to be processed. Create an integer array named pakete and record the weights shown on the packages.
story.packages-loop: Use a simple for loop over pakete. Inside the loop, call roboter.collect(pakete[index]) exactly once for each element so the storage scanner can process the package.
story.data-storage-problem: There is a problem in the data storage room.
story.manual-sorting: The security values are unordered. Inspect the displayed neighboring pair and decide whether the two values must exchange places.
story.bubble-sort-code: The manual sort is complete. Fill in the missing comparison in the prepared Bubble Sort code and save it to the sort chip.
story.archive-intro: We need to build new data stores. Some are missing. Go to the archive and check which arrays the facility requires.
story.archive-arrays: You are in the archive. Inspect the three shelves and create the described arrays in the terminal. The data nodes contain the actual values.
story.storage-unlocked: The two-dimensional storage is now open. An important locator chip must be inside. Find it after you restore the storage.
story.storage-array: You are in the two-dimensional storage. Create an integer grid with three rows and four columns.
story.storage-values: The grid is ready. Several storage cells are marked and contain registered data. Inspect the storage, determine the matching values, and restore those cells in the array.
story.search-program: The locator chip is in the computer. The prepared search currently examines only part of the matrix. Complete the missing row-and-column traversal so every cell can be reached.
story.search-controller: The locator chip is programmed. Insert it into the search robot controller so the search can begin.
story.search-scan: The search robot is active and checking the matrix. Wait until it hands over the system-core module.
story.central-sort: The system core is reachable. Begin by comparing neighboring values and checking whether they are in ascending order.
story.central-count: Now count the occupied entries in modules. Empty entries must not increase the counter.
story.central-search: Finally, search the entire grid. Trigger the robot's collection action whenever a battery signal is found.
story.central-meta: All three routines have reported a result. The central display now combines these values. Open the input mask in the terminal and transfer the combined state there.
story.completed: All checks are confirmed. System recovery can continue.
story.hint-offer: I can provide one additional hint for the active task. It will be recorded in the shared quest log.
story.hint-solution-warning: This is the final hint for the active task. It will reveal the complete solution.
story.hint-none: There are no further hints for the current task. Continue working with the information already recovered.

energy-array.orientation: The damaged regulator needs storage for several energy readings.
energy-array.approach: Use an integer array: one variable can hold several whole numbers with fixed capacity.
energy-array.near: The regulator expects five slots in an array named energie.

energy-values.orientation: Five empty regulator slots need the readings shown in the room.
energy-values.approach: Array indices start at 0. Assign each reading to its matching position; line order is irrelevant.
energy-values.solution: Enter in any order: energie[0] = 40; energie[1] = 10; energie[2] = 80; energie[3] = 30; energie[4] = 60;

energy-insert-battery.orientation: The accepted readings restore power, but the wall battery housing still needs its source.
energy-insert-battery.approach: The lever materializes a battery after the array is correct. Place it in the nearby wall box.
energy-insert-battery.near: Pull the array lever, collect its battery, and insert it into the battery box.
energy-insert-battery.solution: Pull the array lever once, pick up the Battery it spawns, then insert it into the battery box.

module-array.orientation: The next subsystem needs five positions for the facility hardware modules.
module-array.approach: These entries are names, so use an array that stores String values.
module-array.near: Declare a five-slot String array named module.

module-values.orientation: The five module labels in the room identify the values the array needs.
module-values.approach: Store each label as a quoted String at its matching zero-based index; line order is irrelevant.
module-values.near: Assign CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD, NETWORK to module indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
module-values.solution: Enter in any order: module[0] = "CPU"; module[1] = "RAM"; module[2] = "GPU"; module[3] = "SSD"; module[4] = "NETWORK";

module-remove-gpu.orientation: One module reports a fault; the array must show that its slot is empty.
module-remove-gpu.approach: An empty object-array entry is Java null, not the text "null".
module-remove-gpu.near: The failed GPU is at index 2. Assign Java null to that element.

module-length.orientation: The scanner needs the module array's capacity, not its number of occupied entries.
module-length.approach: Java arrays expose capacity through their length field. Clearing an entry does not change it.
module-length.near: Read the length field of the array named module.

room2-door-code.orientation: Two pieces of information from module storage matter for access: the array length and the position of the defective GPU entry.
room2-door-code.approach: Read the length on the display and use the fault index from the GPU record. Write both as two digits; the length comes first.
room2-door-code.near: The array length is 5; the defective GPU is at index 2. Add a leading zero to each value and enter them in order.
room2-door-code.solution: Enter 0502 at the inventory-scanner door keypad.

inventory-count.orientation: The scanner needs the number of modules still installed, not array capacity.
inventory-count.approach: Start a counter at zero, visit each String in module, and increment only for non-null entries.
inventory-count.near: Use an enhanced for loop over module; test entry != null and increment count.
inventory-count.solution: Enter: int count = 0; for (String entry : module) { if (entry != null) { count++; } }

room3-door-code.orientation: Access to transport storage depends on the array capacity and the inventory scan result.
room3-door-code.approach: After the scan, read both values from the display. Write them as two digits each; the array length comes first.
room3-door-code.near: The array length is 5 and four entries are occupied. Write both as two-digit values and enter them in that order.

transport-array.orientation: The storage scanner processes a fixed set of packages whose weights are shown nearby.
transport-array.approach: An integer array literal can hold the weights in conveyor order.
transport-array.near: Create an int array named pakete with 15, 40, 20, 60, 30.

transport-collect-loop.orientation: Every package must pass through the storage scanner exactly once.
transport-collect-loop.approach: Use an index loop from zero to the array length and pass each value to the robot's collect method.
transport-collect-loop.near: Loop while i < pakete.length; call roboter.collect(pakete[i]) once inside.
transport-collect-loop.solution: Enter: for (int i = 0; i < pakete.length; i++) { roboter.collect(pakete[i]); }

data-storage-door-open.orientation: The accepted package sequence is being processed before the next room is accessible.
data-storage-door-open.approach: The conveyor and scanner run automatically now. Watch this world sequence instead of submitting more code.
data-storage-door-open.near: Let the scanner finish; the data-storage door opens when the sequence succeeds.
data-storage-door-open.solution: No code is needed. Wait for the transport scan to finish and door_datenspeicher to open.

manual-sorting.orientation: The data crystals must be ascending; the display compares neighboring values.
manual-sorting.approach: For each pair, decide whether its current order conflicts with ascending order. Choose swap or keep.
manual-sorting.near: Swap only when the left value is greater than the right value.
manual-sorting.solution: Choose TAUSCHEN when left > right; otherwise choose NICHT TAUSCHEN. Continue until the sequence is ascending.

bubble-sort-condition.orientation: The empty sort chip's Bubble Sort program is missing its comparison condition.
bubble-sort-condition.approach: Bubble Sort compares neighbors and swaps them when the left value belongs later in ascending order.
bubble-sort-condition.near: Compare array[j] with array[j + 1] using the greater-than operator.
bubble-sort-condition.solution: Fill the condition with: array[j] > array[j + 1]

bubble-sort-machine.orientation: The sorting machine runs only after a complete program has been saved to its chip.
bubble-sort-machine.approach: Take the programmed chip from the computer and use it on the machine in this room.
bubble-sort-machine.near: Insert the filled chip and let the Bubble Sort cycle finish.
bubble-sort-machine.solution: Use the programmed sort chip on the machine. Wait for the animation, then collect the archive key.

archive-access.orientation: The next records are behind the archive door; the sorting machine produced a key.
archive-access.approach: Use the key as an inventory item on the locked archive door, not as a terminal command.
archive-access.near: Select the archive key and use it on door_datenarchiv.
archive-access.solution: Open inventory, use the archive key on door_datenarchiv, and wait for it to open.

archive-arrays.orientation: The archive describes three data collections missing from the damaged system.
archive-arrays.approach: Create one int array, one String array and one boolean array with the shelf contents.
archive-arrays.solution: Enter: int[] energie = {20, 50, 80}; String[] module = {"CPU", "GPU", "RAM"}; boolean[] aktiv = {true, false, true};

storage-array.orientation: The locator chip is hidden in a storage grid with rows and columns.
storage-array.approach: Use a two-dimensional int array. Its dimensions are row count first, column count second.
storage-array.near: Declare an int[][] named lager with 3 rows and 4 columns.

storage-values.orientation: The shelf markers identify three cells containing numbered data.
storage-values.approach: Address each cell by row then column; both Java indices start at zero.
storage-values.near: Set lager[0][2]=1, lager[1][3]=2 and lager[2][1]=3. Any order is accepted.
storage-values.solution: Enter in any order: lager[0][2] = 1; lager[1][3] = 2; lager[2][1] = 3;

search-program.orientation: The locator must inspect every matrix cell, not only the first column.
search-program.approach: Keep the prepared outer row loop and add an inner loop bounded by the current row length.
search-program.near: For each i, loop j while j < map[i].length. At map[i][j] == 1 call roboter.collect().
search-program.solution: Use: for (int i = 0; i < map.length; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < map[i].length; j++) { if (map[i][j] == 1) { roboter.collect(); } } }

search-robot-run.orientation: The completed locator program must run on the robot before its result is available.
search-robot-run.approach: The programmed chip belongs in the robot controller; then the robot follows the matrix program.
search-robot-run.near: Insert the programmed chip and let the robot finish its scan and deliver the module.
search-robot-run.solution: Use the programmed locator chip on the controller; wait for the search to finish and collect the delivered System Core Access module.

system-core-access.orientation: The central core remains sealed until the recovered access module is executed.
system-core-access.approach: Run the module's release routine at a computer. This is a world interaction, not an array exercise.
system-core-access.near: Insert the System Core Access module into a computer and execute its release script.
system-core-access.solution: At a computer, insert the access module, choose its release program and submit it. door_systemcore opens after server acceptance.

core-sort.orientation: The first core check asks the program to sort an integer array in ascending order.
core-sort.approach: Use Bubble Sort: an outer pass loop, an inner adjacent-pair loop and a temporary variable for swaps.
core-sort.near: Compare array[j] to array[j+1]; if greater, swap via temp. Reduce the inner bound by i.
core-sort.solution: Enter: for (int i = 0; i < array.length - 1; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < array.length - 1 - i; j++) { if (array[j] > array[j + 1]) { int temp = array[j]; array[j] = array[j + 1]; array[j + 1] = temp; } } }

core-count.orientation: The next core check measures how many module slots contain a value.
core-count.approach: Traverse the String array and count only elements that are not null.
core-count.near: Set count to zero, use an enhanced for loop over modules, and increment inside entry != null.
core-count.solution: Enter: int count = 0; for (String module : modules) { if (module != null) { count++; } }

core-search.orientation: The final code check searches a two-dimensional grid for every battery marker.
core-search.approach: Use nested index loops over every row and its length. Check each cell and collect a marker.
core-search.near: When map[i][j] == 1, call roboter.collect(); both loops must cover the full matrix.
core-search.solution: Enter: for (int i = 0; i < map.length; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < map[i].length; j++) { if (map[i][j] == 1) { roboter.collect(); } } }

core-meta.orientation: The three core checks produced separate results. The final form combines them into one system state.
core-meta.approach: Use the sorted energy output, occupied-module count and battery-signal count in their matching fields.
core-meta.near: Enter five ascending energy values; the module count is 3 and battery signals are 3.
core-meta.solution: Submit sortedEnergy={8,17,23,31,42}, activeModules=3 and batterySignals=3 in the three System Core form fields.
